page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-1 is an entry-level general-purpose virtual machine instance within the N1 family. It features 1 dedicated vCPU built on x86_64 Intel Xeon processor architecture running at 2.3 GHz, alongside 4.0 GB of RAM (3.75 GB usable memory per core). The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and 45 MB L3 cache, with instruction set support for AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA. This instance includes no dedicated GPUs, no bundled local storage, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance reflects entry-level throughput suited for modest compute demands. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests yield matching scores of 1088.79. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 10.68 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 9.71 GB/sec. Application tests show 1.21 GB/sec static web serving throughput and 1.29 million Redis SET operations per second. Extended hardware instruction support is constrained, lacking AVX-512 and AMX flags, which limits efficiency in intensive vector or matrix operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the balanced vCPU-to-RAM configuration minimizes hardware overhead for low-intensity applications. The absence of local NVMe drives and GPU hardware reduces total resource costs, though persistent disk attachment is required for storage. The n1-standard-1 is appropriate for lightweight microservices, low-traffic web servers, basic background execution jobs, small caching layers, and development environments.
